answers.explanation: Registers are simplest, but limited in number.
A CPU has a fixed, small number of registers.
The register holds X, where the parameters live in memory.
Push to put on the stack, pop to take off.
Memory has room for as many parameters as needed.
Load address X into a register, then make the call. The kernel's code for call 13 reads its parameters from table X.
Block and stack have no limit; registers alone can't hold 9.
